FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Second Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft finalized 
by the Brushware, Polishes, Lac and Lac Products Sectional Committee has been approved by the Chemical 
Division Council. 


This standard was published in 1964 and revised in 1976. In this revision, PP or nylon (polyamide) has been added 
as the filling material to be used in the manufacturing of brushes in addition to the existing one. Also, all 
amendments have been incorporated in the standard. Further, packing and marking clause has been updated. 


Brushes with palmyra fibre are used by the Indian Railways and other organizations for cleaning of commodes 
and squatting pans, having either short or long chutes. 


The composition of the committee responsible for formulation of this standard is listed in Annex C. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 2022 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision)’. The number of significant places retained 
in the rounded off value shall be same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


Indian Standard 
BRUSH, COMMODE CHUTES — SPECIFICATION 


( Second Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements and the 
methods of sampling and test for brush, commode 
chutes. 


2 REFERENCES 


The following standards contain provisions, which 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions 
of this standard. At the time of publication, the 
editions indicated were valid. All standards are 
subject to revision and parties to agreements based 
on this standard are encouraged to investigate the 
possibility of applying the most recent editions of 
the standards listed below: 


IS No. Title 


IS 707 : 2011 Timber technology and 
utilization of wood, bamboo 
and cane — Glossary of terms 
(third revision) 


IS 1078 :1987 Specification for copper 


naphthenate (second revision) 


IS 1745 : 2018 Petroleum hydrocarbon 
solvents — Specification 


(third revision) 


IS 3451 (Part 2) Code of practice for care and 

: 1975 maintenance of brushes: Part 
2 Brushes other than pan-set 
brushes 


IS 5060 : 1969 . Glossary of terms used in 


brushware industry 


3 TERMINOLOGY 


3.1 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions 
given in IS 5060, IS 707 and the one given below 
shall apply. 


3.1.1 Approved Tender Sample — The sample 
accepted by the indentor or purchaser or inspection 
authority as basis for supply. 


NOTE — When a sample is tested and approved by the 
indentor or purchaser or an inspection authority, the results 
of such tests as will permit the supplier to meet the limits 
imposed by the specification for deliveries shall be made 
available to the supplier. However, all tests need to be 
carried out on the tender sample. 


4 REQUIREMENTS 
4.1 Materials 


Commode chutes brush shall be manufactured from 
the following materials. 


4.1.1 Filling Material 


This shall consist of palmyra (Borassus flabellifer 
Linn., fam. Palmac) fibre which shall be clean, free 
from dust and other extraneous matter or PP or nylon 
(polyamide) of 0.35 mm thickness and the same 
should be manufactured from virgin PP material and 
not recycled. 


As regards colour, luster and stiffness, the filling 
material shall match those used in the approved 
tender sample. The solid dressing of bristles used 
shall be as per the approved tender sample, if so 
agreed to by the indentor. 


4.1.2 Timber 


4.1.2.1 Any of the timber species listed in Annex A 
shall be used in the manufacture of the handle of the 
brush (see Fig. 1). 


4.1.2.2 The timber shall be reasonably 
straight-grained and well-seasoned to a moisture 
content not exceeding 15 percent when tested by the 
moisture meter method. However, in case of dispute 
the oven-dry method shall be used (see Annex B). 


4.1.2.3 The timber shall be free from brashness, any 
kind of biological or non-biological deterioration, 
insect attack, centre heart (pith), knots (except pin 
knots), cracks, warp or any other defect which may 
reduce the life of the brush or affect its utility. 


4.1.3 Twine 


Flax or cotton thread shall be 16 tex x 6 with a single 
thread breaking strength on 50 cm gauge of not less 
than 2.25 kg. 


4.1.4 Staples 
Bright iron wire 0.8 mm 0.2 mm in diameter. 
4.1.5 Cement 


Any suitable weak (10 percent) causticized water- 
resistant cement capable of satisfying the test 
prescribed under 4.5.1 and 4.5.2. 


4.2 Manufacture 


4.2.1 Unless otherwise agreed to between the 
indentor and the manufacturer, the brushes shall 
conform to the shape and design as shown in Fig. 1. 


4.2.2 The head and handle shall be turned from a 
single piece of timber. 


4.2.3 The head shall be drilled with 36 knot holes of 
the shape and size as indicated in Fig. 1. 


4.2.3.1 Cement-set brushes 


The filling material (fibres) shall be properly dipped 
in the cement and firmly tied with twine. After 
tieing, each knot shall be again dipped in the cement 
and properly and securely set to the bottom of the 
knot holes to give the shape of the brush head as 
shown in Fig. 1. 


STAPLE BRIGHT IRON 
WIRE @0.8 + 0.2 mm => 


ENLARGED SECTION X-X 
(HAND MADE) 


*36 Knot holes, 10 mm dia, (13 + 2) mm deep, 7 in 
a row spaced equally around circumference. For the 
first 4 rows of knot holes, drill at 60° + 5° and for 
the fifth row drill at 45° + 5° 


4.2.3.2 Staple set brushes 


The tufts of filling material shall be cross-stapled 
and securely set to the bottom of the knot holes by 
machine, to give the shape of the brush as shown in 
Fig. 1. 


4.3 Dimensions and Tolerances 


The dimensions and tolerances shall be as given in 
Fig. 1. 


4.3.1 A tolerance of + 0.5 mm may be allowed on 
the diameter of the tuft holes. 


ENLARGED SECTION X-X 
(MACHINE MADE) 


SECTION V-V 


All dimensions in millimetres 


Fic. 1 BRUSH COMMODE FOR CHUTES 


4.4 Workmanship and Finish 


4.4.1 The head and handle shall be smoothly 
finished and suitably painted with a 10 percent 
solution of copper naphthenatc (see IS 1078), in 
petroleum hydrocarbon solvent 60/80 (see IS 1745). 


4.4.2 The tuft of the filling material should contain 
filling materials of uniform length and quantity as 
provided in approved tender sample or as agreed to 
between the indentor and the manufacturer. 


4.4.3 In general workmanship and finish, brushes 
shall match the approved tender sample or shall 
satisfy the contract between the indentor and the 
manufacturer. 


4.4.4 The brush handle head should be painted prior 
to fixing the filling material by some protective paint 
which can withstand weak caustic solution. 


4.5 Tests 
The brushes shall satisfy the following tests. 
4.5.1 Soaking Test for Cement-Set Brushes 


Soak the cement-set brushes for two hours in a 
10 percent soap solution maintained at 50 °C + 2 °C. 
After taking out and allowing it to dry, it shall 
conform to the pull test prescribed in 4.5.2 and 4.5.3. 


4.5.2 Pull Test 


When a small tuft of filling material is subjected to 
a straight pull with the thumb and finger grip, the 
same shall not come out. 


4.5.3 Oven Test for Cement-Set Brushes 


The brush, when suspended in an oven with the 
brush head downward and subjected to a 
temperature of 60 °C + 2 °C for 4 h, shall show no 
appreciable creeping of the cement and after cooling 
in the atmosphere for 30 min shall satisfy the pull 
test prescribed under 4.5.2. 


4.5.4 Weight of the Filling Material Per Finished 
Brush 


Unfasten tufts by removal of twine and cement or 
staples. Remove the cement by an appropriate 
solvent and dry in an oven at 100 °C + 2 °C, cool 
and weigh under prevalent atmospheric conditions. 

NOTE — Trichloroethylene or methylene chloride is 


suitable for removing rubber or pitch setting, and acetone 
for synthetic resin settings. 


4.5.4.1 The total mass of the filling material per 
brush shall be a minimum of 120 g. A tolerance of 


+5 percent shall be allowed in the weight of the 
filling material, provided the average mass of the 
filling material per brush in any lot is as specified. 
The average mass of filling material per brush in a 
lot shall be assessed by taking the average mass of 
three brushes in lots not exceeding 300 brushes and 
of six brushes in lots exceeding 300 brushes. 


5 MARKING 


5.1 Unless otherwise agreed to between the indentor 
or inspection authority and the supplier, each brush 
shall be legibly and indelibly marked or stamped 
with the manufacturer's name or recognized 
trademark, if any, and the year of manufacture. 


5.1.1 BIS Certification Marking 


The product may also be marked with the Standard 
Mark. 


5.1.2 The product(s) conforming to the requirements 
of this standard may be certified as per the 
conformity assessment schemes under the 
provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 
2016 and the Rules and Regulations framed there 
under, and the products may be marked with the 
Standard Mark. 


6 PACKING 


6.1 The brushes shall be packed in packages 
mutually agreed to between the indentor or 
inspection authority and the supplier. 


7 SAMPLING 


7.1 The suppliers/manufacturers are required to 
submit three identical tender samples of brushes for 
approval, provided the indent is for more than 
25 brushes, keeping in view that identically similar 
brushes shall have to be supplied to complete the 
indent, in case the same is approved. 


7.2 The indentor or inspection authority shall retain 
one of the three approved tender samples against 
each item till the completion of the order. 


7.3 Representative samples for test shall be drawn as 
prescribed in Annex B. 


8 SHELF LIFE 


8.1 The brushes shall have a shelf life of one year 
from the date of manufacture, provided proper 
storage conditions are used and adequate 
precautions are taken for preserving then as given 
under 4 of IS 3451 (Part 2).

ANNEXB 
(Clause 7) 


SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 


B-1 SCALE OF SAMPLING 
B-1.1 Lot 


In any consignment, all the brushes of the same size 
and quality shall be divided into groups of 
500 brushes or less and each such group shall 
constitute a lot. Care shall be taken to ensure that 
brushes included in a lot do not differ in construction 
as far as possible. 


B-1.2 The conformity of the brushes in a lot to the 
requirements of this specification shall be 
ascertained for each lot separately. The number of 
brushes to be selected for this purpose shall be in 
accordance with Table 1. 


Table 1 Scale of Sampling 
[Clauses C-1.2 and C-1.3 (b)] 


SINo. No. of Brushes No. of Brushes 


in the Lot to be Selected 
N n 
(1) (2) (3) 
i) Up to 10 2 
ii) 11 to 25 3 
iii) 26 to 50 4 
iv) 51 to 100 5 
v) 101 to 150 6 
vi) 151 to 300 7 
vii) 301 to 500 8 


B-1.3 The brushes shall be selected at random. To 
ensure randomness of selection one of the following 
procedures, whichever is suitable, may be followed: 


a) If all the brushes in a lot are packed in one 
box, then starting from any brush, count 
them in any suitable order as 1, 2......up to r 
and so on, where r is the integral part of N/n 
(N and n being the lot size and sample size, 
respectively), Every 7™ brush thus counted 
shall be withdrawn to constitute the sample; 
and 


b) If the brushes in a lot are packed in more than 
one box, approximately equal number of 
brushes shall be picked up at random from 
as many boxes as possible so as to obtain the 
required number of brushes as specified in 
Table 1. 


B-2 CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 


B-2.1 For declaring the conformity of the lot to the 
requirements of this specification, all the brushes 
selected according to B-1.2 and B-1.3 shall satisfy 
the relevant requirements given in 3. 


NOTE — For description of filling materials (see 4.1.1, 
4.1.1.1 and 4.1.1.2) and workmanship and finish (see 4.4), 
the brushes selected shall be matched with the approved 
tender sample, and shall be suitably stamped and sealed by 
the indentor or the inspection authority and the supplier and 
kept at a place agreed to between the two.

Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in.
